results.quote: For any dyadic probability distribution \(\phi=(\phi_1,\dots,\phi_m)\) on the symbols \(s_1\prec\cdots\prec s_m\), we can construct in linear time an alphabetic code C with \(\mathbb{E}[C]\le H(\phi)+1-\phi_1-\phi_m\).

For any non-dyadic probability distribution \(\phi=(\phi_1,\dots,\phi_m)\) on the symbols \(s_1\prec\cdots\prec s_m\) with \(\phi_1,\phi_m>0\), we can construct in linear time an alphabetic code C with \(\mathbb{E}[C]\le H(\phi)+2-\phi_1\left(2-log_2\phi_1-\lceil-log_2\phi_1\rceil\right)-\phi_m\left(2-log_2\phi_m-\lceil-log_2\phi_m\rceil\right)-\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}min(\phi_i,\phi_{i+1})\)

For any non-dyadic probability distribution \(\phi=(\phi_1,\dots,\phi_m)\) on the symbols \(s_1\prec\cdots\prec s_m\), we can construct in linear time an alphabetic code C with \(\mathbb{E}[C]\le H(\phi)+2-\phi_\ell\left(2-log_2\phi_\ell-\lceil-log_2\phi_\ell\rceil\right)-\phi_k\left(2-log_2\phi_k-\lceil-log_2\phi_k\rceil\right)-\sum_{i=\ell}^{k-1}min(\phi_i,\phi_{i+1})+\phi_\ell+\phi_k\)

For any dyadic probability distribution \(\phi=(\phi_1,\dots,\phi_m)\) on the symbols \(s_1\prec\cdots\prec s_m\), we can construct in linear time an alphabetic code C with \(\mathbb{E}[C]\le H(\phi)+2-\phi_1\left(2-log_2\phi_1-\lceil-log_2\phi_1\rceil\right)-\phi_m\left(2-log_2\phi_m-\lceil-log_2\phi_m\rceil\right)-\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}min(\phi_i,\phi_{i+1})\)

results.problem: Alphabetic codes (conditions on first/last two symbols)
results.quote: For any probability distribution \(\phi=(\phi_1,\dots,\phi_m)\) on the symbols \(s_1\prec\cdots\prec s_m\), with \(\phi_1,\phi_2,\phi_{m-1},\phi_m>0\), we can construct in linear time an alphabetic code C with \(\mathbb{E}[C]\le H(\phi)+2-\phi_1(2-log_2\phi_1-\lceil-log_2\phi_1\rceil)-\phi_m(2-log_2\phi_m-\lceil-log_2\phi_m\rceil)-\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}min(\phi_i,\phi_{i+1})-\phi_1max(0,\lceil-log_2\phi_1\rceil-\lceil-log_2\phi_2\rceil-2)-\phi_mmax(0,\lceil-log_2\phi_m\rceil-\lceil-log_2\phi_{m-1}\rceil-2)\)

Let \(\sigma=(\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{2n+1})=(p_0,q_1,p_1,\dots,q_n,p_n)\) be a probability distribution that contains the probabilities \(q_1,\dots,q_n\) and \(p_0,\dots,p_n\) for successful and unsuccessful searches, respectively, on an ordered sequence \(x_1\prec\cdots\prec x_n\). Let C be any alphabetic code for \(\sigma\), of average length \(\mathbb{E}[C]\). Then, one can construct in linear time a binary search tree T for \(\sigma\) of cost \(\mathbb{E}[T]\le\mathbb{E}[C]-\sum_{i=1}^nq_i-\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}min(p_i,p_{i+1})\).

results.problem: Optimal Binary Search Trees (cost upper bound)
results.quote: by using formula (23) of Theorem 3 in formula (36), we get the upper bound \(H(\sigma)+2-\sigma_1-\sigma_{2n+1}-\sum_{i=1}^{2n}min(\sigma_i,\sigma_{i+1})-\sum_{i=1}^nq_i-\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}min(p_i,p_{i+1})\)
